post.caption: 📉 One narrow stretch of sea between Iran and Oman — the Strait of Hormuz — has pushed oil past $100 and moved the price at Ghana's pumps. Here's what's happening, and why you feel it. 🇬🇭

chapters.say: One thin stretch of water between Iran and Oman just pushed up the price of petrol at your pump. Here is what is happening.
The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most important oil gateway, only about thirty three kilometres wide at its narrowest point.
Roughly one in five barrels of the world's oil sails through here every single day. And if it closes, there is almost no other way out.
In late July, Iran attacked a tanker and effectively closed the strait, while United States strikes and Red Sea attacks widened the conflict.
Crude oil shot past one hundred dollars a barrel, up about forty percent in just three weeks.
Ghana buys its fuel in dollars off that same global market. So petrol has climbed to around fourteen cedis, fifty two a litre, with diesel near sixteen.
Whether prices ease now depends on a fragile ceasefire holding. We will keep following this story. Follow GreaterNews, news you can trust.
